A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 28-page versions of the same research work, including Appendices A–D. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original CUB and AwA2 experiments measuring noise effects, SAM training, and concept interventions, with further empirical analyses in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and results, including accuracy comparisons, robustness analyses, and the LLM-generated annotation experiment in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the same SAM training procedure and uncertainty-guided concept intervention strategy in Section 4, with identical objectives and components.

E1.justification: The CUB and AwA2 coverage is unchanged, including synthetic noise scenarios, correlated corruption, and the CUB experiment using LLM-generated annotations in Appendix D.6.

E2.justification: The BASE-versus-SAM comparisons are unchanged. Table 7 retains LSR and SL, and Appendix D.8 retains the same six intervention criteria: Random, UCP, CCTP, LCP, ECTP, and EUDTP.

E3.justification: Section 2.1 and Appendices C–D retain identical data splits, preprocessing, noise-injection procedures, metrics, model configurations, training settings, and intervention protocols.

E4.justification: The susceptibility analyses and Appendix D studies are unchanged, including training-strategy ablations, predictor-complexity comparisons, backbone tests, diverse noise scenarios, and qualitative concept visualizations.

E5.justification: Appendix C.3 states three random seeds and average performance in both versions. The tabulated uncertainty reporting and seed-consistency analysis in Appendix D.13 are unchanged.

E6.justification: All matched numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains CUB task accuracies of 50.35% for BASE and 54.21% for SAM at 20% noise.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, assumptions, propositions, and proofs are identical, including the SAM regularization analysis in Appendix A and uncertainty-ranking justification in Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about systematic noise characterization, susceptible concepts, and mitigation through SAM training and uncertainty-guided intervention.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations in Sections 5–6 and the appendices are unchanged, including uncertainty calibration, linear-predictor limitations, binary-concept scope, and simplified correlated-noise assumptions.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, preprocessing instructions, and code-access information. The acknowledgement edits do not revise technical or resource-access information.

R1.justification: The reference list and research-positioning passages are identical, including the comparisons with prior robustness work in Section 6. No cited works are added or removed.

P1.justification: Page 10 changes 'was supported' to 'was partly supported', replaces IITP grant No.2019-0-01906 with RS-2019-II191906, and removes the No.2022-0-00959 alias. The arXiv version/date stamp also changes; the scientific prose and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–20, Tables 1–11, their captions, and their placement are unchanged. The revised acknowledgement remains within its existing block, without a separate layout redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 changes only the funding acknowledgement and arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific arguments, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and presentation throughout the main text and appendices remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
